Package hadur2.core.physics

Class MovementPredictor

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.physics.MovementPredictor
public class MovementPredictor extends Object
Tick-by-tick prediction of a robot's movement under Robocode's physics, and the precise maximum escape angle built on it.

Wave surfing and guess-factor targeting both ask "where can this robot get to before the bullet arrives?". The classic answer, asin(8 / bulletSpeed), assumes the robot is already at full speed, perpendicular to the shooter, with no walls. This class answers it by simulation instead: predict(hadur2.core.model.RobotState, double, double, double, long, boolean) applies the engine's own turn, acceleration and braking rules one tick at a time, and preciseEscapeAngle(int, Point2D.Double, long, double, RobotState, double, double) drives the robot flat out sideways (smoothing along walls where it has to) until the wave reaches it. hadur2.core.model.Wave uses the result to scale guess factors, and the surf uses the end points as the destinations it compares.

Conventions: angles in radians, 0 north and clockwise; positions in px in field coordinates; velocity in px/tick, negative when reversing; time in ticks. An "orientation" or "direction" of +1 is clockwise round the wave's source, -1 counter-clockwise. The predictor is stateless apart from the field it was built with, so the same inputs always give the same prediction (CORE-2).

  • Method Details

    • predict

      public RobotState predict(RobotState startState, double distance, double turn, double maxVelocity, long ticks, boolean ignoreWalls)
      Simulates a robot for ticks ticks as the engine would move it under setTurnRightRadians(turn), setAhead(distance) and setMaxVelocity(maxVelocity).

      Each tick follows the engine's order: first the body turns, by at most the turn rate allowed at the velocity it had coming into the tick (Rules.getTurnRateRadians(double)); then the velocity changes by at most +1 or -2 px/tick toward what the remaining distance allows (getNewVelocity); then the robot moves that far along its new heading. The remaining turn and distance are used up as it goes.

      If the robot would end a tick outside the field it is pulled back onto the wall along its heading (unless ignoreWalls). As the engine does, it is also stopped dead (PHYS-1): the next tick starts from velocity 0.

      Parameters:
      startState - where the robot starts, with its heading, velocity and time
      distance - how far it is still told to move, in px: negative to reverse, Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY to never brake for a stop
      turn - how far it is still told to turn, in radians, positive clockwise
      maxVelocity - the speed cap it was given, in px/tick
      ticks - how many ticks to simulate
      ignoreWalls - true to let the robot drive through walls (for a hypothetical path whose wall crossing the caller checks itself)
      Returns:
      the state after ticks ticks, with its time advanced by ticks

    • getNewVelocity

      double getNewVelocity(double velocity, double distance, double maxVelocity)
      The velocity after one tick, by the engine's rule: speed up by at most Rules.ACCELERATION, slow down by at most Rules.DECELERATION, never past maxVelocity, and never so fast that the robot could not stop within the remaining distance.

      A robot told to reverse is handled by mirroring: with a negative distance, the answer is the negated answer for the negated velocity and distance. A robot moving backwards that is told to go forwards (velocity < 0) first brakes and then, in the same tick, may start accelerating: see maxDecel.

      Parameters:
      velocity - the velocity coming into the tick, in px/tick
      distance - the distance still to go, in px (negative to reverse, infinite for no stop)
      maxVelocity - the speed cap, in px/tick
      Returns:
      the new velocity, in px/tick

    • nextPerpendicularWallSmoothedLocation

      public RobotState nextPerpendicularWallSmoothedLocation(RobotState robotState, double absBearing, double maxVelocity, double attackAngle, int orientation, double wallStick, boolean ignoreWallHits)
      One tick of driving perpendicular to the line from a wave's source, smoothed along walls. The desired heading is absBearing + orientation × (π/2 + attackAngle): a quarter turn off the bearing is a pure orbit, and since absBearing points away from the source, a positive attack angle turns the heading further round, toward the source.
      Parameters:
      robotState - the robot now
      absBearing - the bearing from the source to the robot, in radians
      maxVelocity - the speed cap, in px/tick
      attackAngle - how far to tilt the path off perpendicular, in radians: positive toward the source, negative away
      orientation - +1 to drive clockwise round the source, -1 counter-clockwise
      wallStick - the wall-smoothing stick length, in px; 0 turns smoothing off
      ignoreWallHits - true to let the robot drive through walls
      Returns:
      the robot one tick on

    • nextLocation

      public RobotState nextLocation(RobotState robotState, double maxVelocity, double goAngle, boolean ignoreWallHits)
      One tick of driving toward goAngle, back-as-front: if the heading is more than a quarter turn from it, the robot turns the short way and drives in reverse, as DiaUtils.setBackAsFront(hadur2.core.model.BotOrders.Builder, double, double) orders it to. The distance is a nominal 1000 px either way, far enough that the braking rule never slows the robot in the one tick simulated.
      Parameters:
      robotState - the robot now
      maxVelocity - the speed cap, in px/tick
      goAngle - the direction to move in, in radians
      ignoreWallHits - true to let the robot drive through walls
      Returns:
      the robot one tick on

    • preciseEscapeAngle

      public MaxEscapeTarget preciseEscapeAngle(int predictDirection, Point2D.Double sourceLocation, long fireTime, double bulletSpeed, RobotState startState, double attackAngle, double wallStick)
      The precise maximum escape angle in one direction: how far round the source, seen from it, the robot can get before the wave reaches it, if it drives flat out sideways.

      First the robot drives in a straight line perpendicular to its bearing at fire time (a line, not an orbit: the bearing is not updated) until the wave passes it or it leaves the field. If it stays in the field, that is the answer: nothing gets further in the time. If it hits a wall, the wall-smoothed search is tried too, and whichever gets the wider angle wins. The surf takes the end location as the destination of that direction's option; the guns and waves take the angle as the escape angle a guess factor of ±1 stands for.

      Parameters:
      predictDirection - +1 to escape clockwise round the source, -1 counter-clockwise
      sourceLocation - where the wave was fired from
      fireTime - the tick the wave was fired
      bulletSpeed - the wave's speed, in px/tick; must exceed 8 so the wave catches the robot
      startState - the robot at the start of the prediction
      attackAngle - how far to tilt the path off perpendicular, in radians: positive toward the source, negative away
      wallStick - the wall-smoothing stick length, in px
      Returns:
      the widest escape found: its angle in radians (positive in predictDirection), the robot's end location (inside the field), the tick it gets there, and hitWall true only when the straight run is returned and it met a wall

    • straightPreciseEscapeAngle

      MaxEscapeTarget straightPreciseEscapeAngle(int predictDirection, double absBearing, Point2D.Double sourceLocation, long fireTime, double bulletSpeed, RobotState startState, double attackAngle)
      The straight run of the precise escape angle: drive at full speed along the fixed perpendicular heading (walls ignored) until the robot leaves the field or the wave passes it. It always ends, since the robot leaves the field eventually. The end point is clamped into the field, so a run that hit a wall reports the angle to the wall.
      Parameters:
      predictDirection - +1 clockwise round the source, -1 counter-clockwise
      absBearing - the bearing from the source to the robot at the start, in radians
      sourceLocation - where the wave was fired from
      fireTime - the tick the wave was fired
      bulletSpeed - the wave's speed, in px/tick
      startState - the robot at the start
      attackAngle - the tilt off perpendicular, in radians, positive toward the source
      Returns:
      the angle reached (positive in predictDirection), where and when, and whether the run left the field

    • smoothingPreciseEscapeAngle

      MaxEscapeTarget smoothingPreciseEscapeAngle(int predictDirection, double absBearing, Point2D.Double sourceLocation, long fireTime, double bulletSpeed, RobotState startState, double attackAngle, double wallStick, int iterations)
      The wall-smoothed run of the precise escape angle, for when the straight run meets a wall. Each pass drives at full speed from startState, back-as-front, re-smoothing the heading against the walls every tick, until the wave passes the robot. The first pass starts from the smoothed perpendicular heading; each later pass starts by heading straight at the point the previous pass reached, then smooths from there. The widest angle over all passes is kept, so an extra pass can only widen the answer.

      Only the wave's passing ends a pass, so this relies on the wave outrunning the robot (bulletSpeed above 8 px/tick, true of every legal bullet, whose speed is 11 or more).

      Parameters:
      predictDirection - +1 clockwise round the source, -1 counter-clockwise
      absBearing - the bearing from the source to the robot at the start, in radians
      sourceLocation - where the wave was fired from
      fireTime - the tick the wave was fired
      bulletSpeed - the wave's speed, in px/tick
      startState - the robot at the start
      attackAngle - the tilt off perpendicular, in radians, positive toward the source
      wallStick - the wall-smoothing stick length, in px
      iterations - how many passes to make
      Returns:
      the widest angle reached (0 at the start location if none was positive), where and when; hitWall is always false
